label: Ground-motion model

instance_schema.description: One GMM per parameter set: its functional form, the IM it predicts, and that form's coefficients. A form is a kernel in src/builder/kernels/hazard.py (GMM_FORMS); a set of numbers for an existing form needs no code.

form.description: The functional form these coefficients belong to.

imt.description: The intensity measure this set predicts.

sigma.description: Aleatory ln standard deviation: a + b*Mw below m_break, sigma_above at or above it.

source.note: Each parameter set cites its own model. The kernel holds the functional forms.

description: ln IM at the bridges as one Gaussian field, ln IM ~ N(mu, D R D) with D = diag(sigma): mu, the median ln IM at each bridge from the event's magnitude and the bridge's distance, and sigma, the GMM's total standard deviation, for whichever GMM the parameter set is. R is the binding's correlation (a spatial-correlation set); without one the bridges are independent, which the result says. The event is fixed data: the one Event row's mw, lat, lon and depth_km, read like the bridge's own lat/lon, so it is no BN node. An uncertain rupture (e.g. sampled from a source model) would come back as a scenario function feeding an input here. Choose the set with parameter_set_by_location to use the model made for where the network is. Joint: one draw covers every bridge. Campbell (2003) gives one total sigma, without the between- and within-event split that correlating it properly needs.
